تَنْبِيتٌ and ↓ تِنْبِيتٌ , (K,) the latter so written, not as being so originally, but for the sake of agreement in sound [with respect to the first and second vowels], (AHei,) a subst., signifying What grows or germinates, of slender (i. e. small, TA,) trees, [or shrubs,] and large: (K:) ex., “بَيْدَآءُ لَمْ يَنْبُتْ بِهَا تَنْبِيتُ
” [A desert in which there grew not aught of shrubs or of large trees]: (TA:) young shoots of palmtrees: (IKtt:) the prickles and branches that are cut off from a palm-tree, to lighten it. (AHn, as from 'Eesa Ibn-'Omar.) ―
-b2- Pieces of the hump of a camel. (L.)
From An Arabic-English Lexicon (Edward William Lane)
